answer: Divergent Nonce Beacon. Each identity gets a random starting value (beacon) and must publish a fresh, unpredictable successor each epoch, forming a signed chain. A clone can only copy the original's replies, so it cannot produce a distinct successor when the network probes both at once. Honest agents derive successors from private entropy plus a per-round vertex in a shared hash graph; copying forces an attacker to sync every clone to one source, collapsing them into a single detectable falcon trajectory. Cost: one full state-sync per clone per epoch plus loss of all independent forks.
